correctness.rationale: The Euler-product identity is exact. For at least two prime-power blocks, replacing the remaining factor product by \(1\) gives a valid lower bound, and expansion yields \(p^{a-1}q^{b-1}(q^{b+1}+p^{a+1}-1)\ge12\). Equality forces exactly the blocks \(2\) and \(3\). Prime powers satisfy \(F(p^a)=p^{a-1}\), so the low-fiber enumeration is exhaustive.

value.rationale: The exact sequence already distinguishes primes and prime powers, so the first mixed-support value is a natural invariant. The theorem proves that invariant is \(12\), uniquely at \(6\), and thereby determines the full spectrum through the transition from prime-power to mixed support.
